subject: general
question: Which of the following is an example of GUI-based user agent in email?
solution:
The correct answer is **Netscape**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Netscape:

 
• Netscape refers to Netscape Navigator, which was a popular web browser that included a built-in email client called Netscape Messenger.
 
• Netscape Messenger was a GUI-based email client, providing a graphical interface where users could interact with buttons, menus, and other graphical elements

Elm:

 
• Elm is a text-based email client used on Unix systems. It provides a simple, menu-driven system for managing email, and it operates entirely in the terminal or console window.
 
• Elm uses a text-based user interface, not a graphical one

Mail:

 
• This is a bit ambiguous as "Mail" could refer to several different programs.
 
• However, in most contexts, especially older ones, "Mail" refers to a simple command-line-based mail program on Unix-like systems.
 
• This is also text-based and operates via command line without a graphical interface.

Pine:

 
• Pine, like Elm, is another text-based email client for Unix-like systems.
 
• It offers a slightly more user-friendly approach compared to older text-based email clients but still operates within a text-based environment.
